nodes.title: Selberg optimal weights
nodes.statement: For a native BoundingSieve s and real z>1, put G(s,z)=Σ_{d|P,d<z} s.selbergTerms(d). Define λ_z(d)=μ(d)/(ν(d)G(s,z)) times Σ_{l|P,d|l,l<z} s.selbergTerms(l) for d|P and d<z, and zero otherwise. Then G>0, λ_z(1)=1 and |λ_z(d)|≤1 on divisors of P. The native quadratic form has minimum 1/G among all weights supported on d<z and normalized at 1.
hypotheses: P is the native squarefree prodPrimes and 0<ν(p)<1 on its prime factors.
The cutoff is strict d<z. z>1 is essential: at z=1 the d=1 term is absent.
Optimization concerns the main term, not the absolute remainder; the latter remains separate.
proofSteps: Use the native diagonalization, rather than introducing a second quadratic form.
Möbius inversion of y_l=Σ_{d|P,l|d}ν(d)λ(d) gives the displayed λ when y_l=μ(l)g(l)/G for l<z.
Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives 1≤G times the diagonal form because λ(1)=1. The displayed y attains equality.
For the modulus bound, factor the coprime Euler sums and compare the numerator with G.
acceptance: Keep every stated hypothesis and the indicated strict or inclusive endpoints; the node is a plan, not an implementation claim.

nodes.title: Bouniakowsky and Schinzel hypotheses
nodes.statement: For f∈ℤ[X], IsBouniakowskyPolynomial means positive leading coefficient and, for every prime p, an integer n with p∤f(n). IsSchinzelTuple means every entry has positive leading coefficient and, for each p, one n avoids divisibility in every entry. BouniakowskyAdmissible and SchinzelAdmissible additionally require irreducibility of each polynomial. The Bouniakowsky conjecture and Schinzel H assert infinitely many natural arguments yielding positive primes for every admissible polynomial or tuple. These conjectures are named hypotheses, never asserted.
hypotheses: Polynomials are in the native Polynomial ℤ carrier.
The local condition is on the product, with a common n for each prime; separate admissibility is insufficient.
The empty tuple has the vacuous simultaneous-primality condition. Constant irreducible polynomials are excluded automatically by the local condition.
proofSteps: Use native irreducibility, leadingCoeff and evaluation; define only the admissibility and conjecture predicates.
For an integer polynomial, evaluation modulo p depends only on n modulo p. The residue formulation agrees by lifting residues.
The singleton tuple is exactly the Bouniakowsky case; finite products express the shared local condition.
acceptance: Keep every stated hypothesis and the indicated strict or inclusive endpoints; the node is a plan, not an implementation claim.

nodes.title: Squared finite large-sieve duality
nodes.statement: For finite index sets I,J, a complex matrix A and C≥0, the inequality Σ_i |Σ_j A_ij a_j|²≤CΣ_j|a_j|² for every a is equivalent to Σ_j |Σ_i conjugate(A_ij)b_i|²≤CΣ_i|b_i|² for every b. The conjugate is essential; C is the squared norm bound.
hypotheses: I,J finite; C≥0.
proofSteps: Realize the finite matrix as a continuous map between native finite l² spaces.
A squared inequality is equivalent to the operator norm being at most √C. Apply the native isometric adjoint and its involutivity; expand its coordinates.

The empty coefficient interval is handled separately by zero, not by extending a negative constant.
hypotheses: N≥1; 0<δ≤1/2; finite frequency family; circular separation.
proofSteps: Use the Hilbert inequality to control the off-diagonal geometric kernel, retaining both endpoints of the interval.

nodes.title: Binary polynomial local densities
nodes.statement: For Q∈Z[x₀,x₁] and a>0, ρ_Q(a) counts zeros in (Z/aZ)², with ρ_Q(0)=0. For prime p and k≥1 a zero modulo p^k is smooth if some partial derivative is nonzero modulo p. Let ρsing_Q(p^k) count the remaining zeros, and let ρ̃_Q(p^k) count zeros which are smooth OR have no zero lift modulo p^(k+1). Extend ρ̃ multiplicatively to positive a, with ρ̃(1)=1 and ρ̃(0)=0. Do not replace it by a smooth-only count.
hypotheses: Native two-variable polynomial over Z; positive moduli for counts; p prime and k≥1 for the singular correction.
proofSteps: Use finite native residue spaces and polynomial evaluation; define the reduction of a lift coordinatewise.
The corrected prime-power density explicitly includes singular points with no lift. Use prime factorization for its multiplicative extension.
acceptance: Keep every stated hypothesis and the indicated strict or inclusive endpoints; the node is a plan, not an implementation claim.

nodes.title: Curve lifting and singular correction
nodes.statement: For prime p,k≥1, every smooth zero modulo p^k has exactly p zero lifts to p^(k+1); a singular zero has either p² lifts or no lift. Thus p²ρ̃_Q(p^k)=p²ρ_Q(p^k)−ρsing_Q(p^(k+1)).
hypotheses: p prime; k≥1.
proofSteps: Taylor-expand Q at x+p^k t modulo p^(k+1); higher terms vanish for k≥1.
Count solutions to the resulting one linear equation in two F_p coordinates. Smoothness gives p solutions; a zero gradient gives all or none.
Singular zeros upstairs all reduce to singular points, giving the correction formula.

nodes.title: Binary sieve Euler denominator
nodes.statement: For each integer degree bound d≥1 there is c_d>0 such that a nonnegative multiplicative g with 0≤g(p)≤d satisfies Σ_{n≤z} μ(n)²g(n)/n≥c_d ∏_{d<p≤z}(1−g(p)/p)⁻¹ for z>1. The source starts with arbitrary real d>0; the integer version suffices for polynomial degree.
hypotheses: Native multiplicative arithmetic function; nonnegative; prime values bounded by d; z>1.
proofSteps: Extend g’s prime values completely multiplicatively and compare with h(p)=d−g(p). Their squarefree Dirichlet convolution is d^ω.
Use the squarefree d^ω/n lower estimate and the Mertens product comparison; both exact uniform analytic inputs are requested from AN.2.
acceptance: Keep every stated hypothesis and the indicated strict or inclusive endpoints; the node is a plan, not an implementation claim.

nodes.title: Binary-form large sieve on convex domains
nodes.statement: For a planar domain in L(C_l,θ), area A≥1 and radius R>0, θ∈(0,2], and 2≤z≤min((A/R^θ)^(1/5),A^(1/4)), the number of integer points with positive Q-value and no prime p<z dividing that value is at most C A∏_{deg Q<p<z}(1−ρ_Q(p)/p²). C depends only on degree and C_l. This safe-cutoff version uses p<z consistently; the paper’s wider A^(1/2) range is an explicit gap until its lcm discrepancy step is justified.
hypotheses: Q mod p nonzero for every p<z; L-domain input; θ≤2; safe lcm cutoff z²≤√A.
proofSteps: Apply the generic finite Gram-row sieve to the two-dimensional residue characters, with squarefree moduli at most z.
For m,n≤z, the lcm is at most z²≤√A, so the L-domain discrepancy is applicable. Account for the area versus #E normalization: there are two discrepancy contributions.
Sum n·lcm(m,n)² times these errors to obtain O(C_l R^θ z^5); the stated cutoff absorbs it into A.
Use the Euler denominator node and the native Schwartz–Zippel adapter. The wider printed cutoff is not asserted by this node.
acceptance: Keep every stated hypothesis and the indicated strict or inclusive endpoints; the node is a plan, not an implementation claim.

nodes.title: Binary sieve cutoff comparison
nodes.statement: For a polynomial of degree d≥1, z≥2 and s≥1, with content primes omitted on both sides, ∏_{d<p<z^(1/s)}(1−ρ_Q(p)/p²)≤C_d s^d ∏_{d<p<z}(1−ρ_Q(p)/p²). Constants depend only on d. Requiring s≥1 removes the false vanishing right side as s tends to zero.
hypotheses: s≥1; z≥2; nonzero reduction at every included prime.
proofSteps: Use Schwartz–Zippel to bound the local factors and a uniform Mertens estimate between the two cutoffs. Bound primes in the fixed small range separately.

nodes.title: Binary polynomial sieve at power level
nodes.statement: If A≥1, R^θ≤A^(1−η), 0<η<1/2, θ∈(0,2], and 1≤z≤A^ς for fixed ς>0, the positive-value rough-point count is ≤C A∏_{deg Q<p<z}(1−ρ_Q(p)/p²), with C depending only on degree,C_l,η,ς. Content primes below z give an empty sifted set.
hypotheses: L(C_l,θ) domain; polynomial nonzero; η∈(0,1/2); ς>0; positive Q-values.
proofSteps: Apply the safe-cutoff large sieve at z₀=min(z,A^(η/5)); since η<1/2 this also satisfies z₀≤A^(1/4).
The rough-point set decreases as the cutoff increases. Compare Euler products with s=max(1,5ς/η), retaining all constant dependence. Handle bounded area directly.

nodes.title: Binary sieve with divisibility conditions
nodes.statement: For A≥1, R^θ≤A^(1−3η), η∈(0,1/2), θ∈(0,2], a≥1 with a≤A^η, and 1≤z≤A^ς, the count of points with a|Q, gcd(a,Q/a)=1 and Q/a positive and z-rough is at most C Aρ̃_Q(a)/a² times ∏_{deg Q<p<z,p∤a}(1−ρ_Q(p)/p²). Without the gcd condition use ordinary ρ_Q(a).
hypotheses: L-domain as above; positive quotient; integer a≥1; fixed ς>0.
proofSteps: Split into the zero residue classes modulo a and rescale the domain by a.
The gcd condition removes precisely the classes with maximal singular lifts, leaving corrected density; removing the condition retains every zero class.
At primes not dividing a the translated quotient polynomial has the same local count. Check the rescaled area and radius inequalities before applying the level theorem.

nodes.title: Multiplicative decoupling inequality
nodes.statement: For nonnegative multiplicative native arithmetic functions g,ψ, h=ζ*ψ, integer Z≥1 and prime-power tails Σ_{j≥v}g(p^j) summable, Σ_{a≤Z}g(a)h(a)≤Σ_{a≤Z}g(a)·∏_{p≤Z}[1+Σ_{1≤v≤floor(log Z/log p)}ψ(p^v)Σ_{j≥v}g(p^j)]. A finite-tail version with the full admissible exponent cutoff avoids unnecessary convergence assumptions.
hypotheses: Nonnegative multiplicative functions; positive Z; summability required for real infinite sums.
proofSteps: Expand the native divisor convolution. Write the cofactor as a part supported on primes of the divisor and a coprime part.

Use multiplicativity for the coprime part, enlarge its finite sum, and factor the remaining nonnegative sum by primes. Infinite tails are justified by monotone finite truncation and the stated summability.

nodes.title: Average absorption of the density correction
nodes.statement: Assume ρ̃_Q(p^k)≤C p^{k(2−r)}, C>0,0<r≤1, and a nonnegative multiplicative f with f(n)≤B n^ε for n>0, B>0,0<ε<r. Then Σ_{a≤z} f(a)ρ̃_Q(a)θ_Q(a)/a²≤C′Σ_{a≤z}f(a)ρ̃_Q(a)/a² for every z≥1, with C′ depending only on degree,B,C,r,ε.
hypotheses: Positive arguments; corrected local bound on every prime power.
proofSteps: Apply decoupling with g=fρ̃/a² and ψ=λ_Q.
Only v=1 contributes because λ_Q is squarefree. Each prime correction is O(p^(−1−r+ε)); sum the convergent Euler corrections with uniform constants.

nodes.title: Binary multiplicative-function sieve
nodes.statement: For a domain in L(C_l,θ), A≥1,R^θ≤A^(1−3η), η∈(0,1/2), θ∈(0,2], positive polynomial values ≤X≤A^δ with X≥1,δ>0, corrected densities ρ̃_Q(p^k)≤C p^{k(2−r)},C>0,0<r≤1, and f∈M(A_f,B,ε) with 0<ε<min(r,ηr/(4δ)), the sum of f(Q) over integer points is ≤C′ A∏_{deg Q<p≤X,p not content}(1−ρ_Q(p)/p²)Σ_{a≤X}f(a)ρ̃_Q(a)/a². C′ depends only on the listed fixed parameters and degree.
hypotheses: Positive Q-values explicitly required because f is defined on naturals; every analytic parameter and bound shown above.
proofSteps: Split each value at the longest increasing-prime-power prefix below A^η, keeping the coprime factorization.
Bound rough complementary factors by divisibility sieving; absorb θ_Q on average. Very smooth factors use the two averaging savings.

nodes.title: Integral local normal forms for conic counts
nodes.statement: For primitive q=ax²+bxy+cy² of negative discriminant D=b²−4ac, the existing integral-local classification specializes to the following count-preserving changes of variables over Z_p: diagonal ux²+Ay² with u a unit if p is odd or p=2,D≡0 mod4; xy if p=2,D≡1 mod8; x²+xy+y² if p=2,D≡5 mod8. Reduce the isometries modulo every p^n to obtain bijections of the counted residue spaces. This imports the local classification, rather than planning Jordan theory again.
hypotheses: Primitive q; D<0; integral GL₂(Z_p) equivalence, not just equivalence over Q_p.
proofSteps: Import integral localization, odd-prime orthogonal bases and dyadic unimodular classification from the current IntegralLattices Layer 3.

Supply the specific rank-two half-norm adapter and its reductions modulo p^n. Its exact coefficient/discriminant normalization is a gap; rational quadratic-form diagonalization alone does not suffice.

nodes.title: Regular-prime conic densities
nodes.statement: For primitive q of discriminant D<0, Q=q−ωD, prime p with p∤ωD and n≥1, ρ_Q(p^n)=ρ̃_Q(p^n)=p^(n−1)(p−χ_D(p)), where χ_D is the Kronecker discriminant character. At 2 use the explicit dyadic value, not the native odd Jacobi convention.
hypotheses: Primitive q; D<0; p∤ωD; n≥1.
proofSteps: The reduction is smooth; count the projective conic and remove its zero, one or two points at infinity according to the splitting character.
For p=2 use xy or x²+xy+y² directly: their nonzero-level affine counts are respectively 1 and 3. Every zero is smooth and each lift multiplies the count by p.

nodes.title: Singular-prime conic density recursion
nodes.statement: For odd p and a nondegenerate unit binary quadratic form q₀, let R(n,m) count q₀(x,y)≡u₃p^m mod p^n, with u₃ a unit. Set R(0,m)=1; R(n,0)=p^(n−1)(p−χ) where χ is its discriminant Legendre symbol. For m≥1 its smooth part is (p−1)(1+χ)p^(n−1); its singular part is p²R(n−2,m−2) when n,m≥2, zero for n≥2,m=1, and 1 for n=1. For a diagonal conic with p^ℓ exactly dividing D, n≤ℓ gives ρ_Q(p^n)=p^(n+floor(n/2)). For n>ℓ, rescale x=p^ceil(ℓ/2)x₀ and use the equation u p^(ℓ mod2)x₀²+u_Ay²+4ωu u_A≡0 mod p^(n−ℓ), with multiplicity p^(ℓ+floor(ℓ/2)).
hypotheses: Odd prime p; unit coefficients; primitive conic; ℓ is the actual valuation of D. Dyadic diagonal case uses a separate bound.
proofSteps: Separate primitive residue pairs from pairs divisible by p. For a split form the nonzero zero-level fibre has 2(p−1) points; for an anisotropic form it has none.
Scaling pairs divisible by p gives the exact recursion. This corrects the source’s 1−χ where (p−1)(1+χ) is required.
In the ramified normal form, 2ceil(ℓ/2)−ℓ is ℓ mod2, not twice that number, and Q=q−ωD gives the plus sign before 4ωu u_A. Count the free discarded digits explicitly.
acceptance: p=3,q₀=x²−y²,m=n=1 gives5 roots, not1.
p=3,q=x²+3y²,ω=1,n=2 gives0 roots; at n=1 all3 roots are non-lifting.

nodes.title: Uniform conic local-density bound
nodes.statement: For primitive integral q=ax²+bxy+cy² of D<0, any integer ω, prime p and n≥1, ρ_{q−ωD}(p^n)≤16 p^(3n/2); therefore the same bound holds for corrected densities and supplies r=1/2,C=16. Constants do not depend on q,D,ω.
hypotheses: Primitive q; D<0; every prime, including 2; n≥1.
proofSteps: A primitive binary quadratic has a primitive vector of unit value modulo p, so an integral basis change makes its leading coefficient a unit.

For each second coordinate, bound the roots of the resulting unit-leading quadratic modulo p^n by a constant times p^(n/2), using valuation and square-root lifting; retain the dyadic loss in the constant 16. Sum over p^n second coordinates.
This direct finite-root argument is preferable to relying on the source’s incorrect singular closed forms; the exact dyadic root bound and integral normal-form adapter remain proof-closure gaps.

nodes.title: Genus-restricted conic density sum
nodes.statement: For odd p, unit integers u,u_A, q=ux²+p u_Ay², D=−4u u_Ap, p∤ω, ε=±1, and k=0 or1, sum ρ_{q−ωD}(p^k a;p²) over unit a mod p^(2−k) with (a/p)=ε. For k=0 the sum is p³(p−1) if (u/p)=ε and 0 otherwise. For k=1 it is p²[p−1−ε(u_A/p)−(−ωu/p)]/2. The last sign is required by the source’s definition Q=q−ωD.
hypotheses: p odd prime; u,u_A,ω units mod p; ε=±1; congruence local counts as ρ_{Q−t}(modulus).
proofSteps: Introduce a nonzero square variable w so that p^k a=p^k u_εw², and divide the resulting count by the exact multiplicity 2p^k.
For k=0 every contributing point is smooth. For k=1 reduce the correctly signed equation to u_Ay²−u_εw²+4ωu u_A=0 modulo p, subtract w=0, and count free lifted digits.

The paper’s final factor has (ωu/p) in place of (−ωu/p). A finite check at p=3,u=u_A=ω=1,k=1,ε=−1 gives 18 for the actual count and 9 for the printed factor. The corrected formula is a finite-count specialization, not a global genus theory.

nodes.title: Quadratic-order ideal counts in the growth class
nodes.statement: For a fixed imaginary quadratic order Λ, let r_Λ(n) be the number of integral invertible Λ-ideals of norm n, with r_Λ(0)=0. Import that carrier and its norm fibres from the existing order/Picard and arithmetic Dirichlet-series roadmaps. The sieve specialization proves r_Λ is multiplicative and belongs to M(A_Λ,B_{Λ,ε},ε) for every ε>0, with the conductor-prime factors treated explicitly. For maximal orders one may take the standard divisor-count majorant.

nodes.title: Maximal Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem

Native finite norm fibres, number-field ideal divisor/logarithmic coefficient bounds and prime-power removal. The principal-class prime asymptotic is a separate Chebotarev request, not inferred from ideal-counting or generic Tauberian infrastructure.

Strong approximation for a finitely generated Zariski-dense subgroup at almost all squarefree moduli, including the exact reduction-image/CRT statement and the finite bad modulus; not just density of all G(Q).
Uniform Lang–Weil counts for the group and geometric hypersurface zero loci/intersections, and proper-subvariety O(p^(dimG−1)) reduction counts.

BGS Theorem1.3 squarefree-ring sum-product with every large-divisor projection hypothesis, and the noncommutative Balog–Szemerédi–Gowers/product-growth inputs of the SL₂ flattening argument. Only these general combinatorial results are requested; the affine sieve and its expansion application remain SV.5 targets.
Convergence and positivity of ∏_(odd prime p)(1−1/(p−1)²), and its role as the dimension-one local factor for Goldbach.

The zero-free bounds for primitive Dirichlet L-functions and contour estimates used in Chen1973 Lemma6; specify the small-conductor range d≤log¹⁰⁰N, the L′/L line and smoothing before the M₂ bound is used.

The native Hilbert product formula, with the local quadratic-character identification at odd primes and the finite dyadic/infinite factors. SV.5 specializes it to (α/(β))(β/(α))=∏_(v|2∞)(α,β)_v for coprime odd elements, and then to the joint-spin kernel residue sign; it does not reconstruct local or global reciprocity.

Apply the natural prime-count asymptotic to the identity Frobenius class in the Hilbert class field, using ClassFieldTheory’s principal-ideal splitting criterion. This gives #{principal prime ideals with norm≤X}∼li(X)/h_K, with finite bad primes and higher-residue-degree terms removed. Dirichlet density alone is insufficient.

gaps.title: Mass and remainder control in Eratosthenes applications
gaps.detail: The unconditional source example behind E7 needs a relation between approximate mass X, the divisor cutoff and absolute remainder mass. The new conditional theorem requires the concrete inequalities it uses. Establish those inequalities for any proposed application rather than inferring them from a sieve carrier or a level parameter.

gaps.title: Integral conic normal-form comparison
gaps.detail: Import IntegralLattices Layer 3 local classification. Supply the rank-two half-norm adapter from q=ax²+bxy+cy², including the dyadic discriminant cases, integral GL₂(Z_p) changes and bijections modulo every p^n. The pinned baseline has no assembled interface for this comparison; the native theorem prototype is omitted.

gaps.title: Uniform dyadic conic root bound
gaps.detail: Prove that a unit-leading quadratic modulo 2^n has at most a fixed constant times 2^(n/2) roots uniformly in its remaining coefficients, including repeated-root valuations. Sum over the second coordinate and track the factor16. Odd-prime finite regressions do not establish this bound.

gaps.title: Conductor-local invertible-ideal counting
gaps.detail: GlobalNumberFields Layer 11 and ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer 1 supply the order-ideal carrier and norm fibres. The missing input is a conductor-prime formula bounding r_Λ(p^k) for all k with fixed-order constants, and its coprime norm multiplicativity. Native order-count prototype omitted until that interface exists.

gaps.title: Curvature-uniform lattice discrepancy
gaps.detail: GN.4 must supply the scaled and translated planar lattice estimate at every modulus actually used: area A/a²≥1 and error C(R/a)^θ. The sharp Huxley/van der Corput ranges require their own regularity hypotheses. The binary large-sieve proof uses lcm(m,n)≤sqrt(A), hence the conservative z≤A^(1/4) cutoff.

gaps.title: Uniform binary Euler and smooth-factor estimates
gaps.detail: Complete degree-uniform squarefree Euler lower bounds, the absorption of θ_Q after increasing the growth exponent, and the two smooth-factor savings with constants depending only on the stated growth, density and degree parameters. AN.2 and AN.5 requests specify the prime-product and smooth-number inputs; their existence is not inferred from the finite Rankin lemmas.

gaps.title: Ordinary-density input in the binary main sieve
gaps.detail: Theorem9.7 proof equation(47), p.233, bounds an R₂ contribution using ordinary ρ_Q(p^e) at strength O(p^e). Its hypothesis only bounds corrected densities by Cp^{e(2−r)}. Q=x₀² gives ρ_Q(p²)=p³, so the asserted ordinary bound is unavailable. Repair R₂ at the stated generality, or state and propagate a justified additional hypothesis. The intended main conclusion is retained as a planning target, not asserted proved.

gaps.title: Corrected congruence transport for the binary sieve
gaps.detail: Reconstruct Propositions9.25–9.26 after scaling. Retain (R/k₀)^θ≤(A/k₀²)^(1−3η), the transformed value bound, and local class Q≡k₀k₁ℓ mod k₁k₂. Show precisely how corrected densities of Q_r/k₀ recombine at primes dividing k₀, and how the coprime unit residue is transported. A formal substitution in the printed formulas is insufficient.

gaps.title: Uniform Selberg denominator asymptotics
gaps.detail: AN.2 supplies prime sums/PNT and the requested Wirsing asymptotic. Prove positivity and the Γ(κ+1) Euler normalization of H_g, and uniformity when progression-modulus primes are removed. Track the log interval and totient factors for the interval, progression and dimension-two applications.

gaps.title: Restricted Halberstam–Richert input in the Maynard route
gaps.detail: GGPY §2 Lemma3 cites Halberstam–Richert Lemmas5.3–5.4. That book is not cleared and was not read. gaps.title: Sharp Hilbert and additive large-sieve proofs
gaps.detail: Kedlaya Chapter15 leaves the separated real-line Hilbert inequality and endpoint improvement as exercises. Prove the π/δ Hilbert constant, the periodic/circular adapter and H−1+δ⁻¹ inequality, including arbitrary interval origin, H≥1 and singleton cases. Squared matrix duality alone supplies no sharp constant.
